conventions.convention: Policy parameters lie in an open Euclidean domain; each state has a fixed nonempty supported action set, positive throughout that domain, and the score is the gradient of the logarithm only on supported actions.
Episodes stop at the first terminal state; 0 ≤ γ < 1; G_t discounts relative to time t, whereas the start-state gradient estimator includes the additional factor γ^t.
The score is zero after termination, and conditioning is on the entire history through the current state before sampling its action.

The episodic gradient theorem assumes AC, almost-sure termination in a parameter neighborhood, summably dominated return-weighted likelihood remainders, absolute convergence of the derivative sum, and integrability of the discounted score-reward double sum.
REINFORCE freezes the generating parameter throughout an episode and evaluates every score at that same parameter before making one accumulated update.
The baseline is a fixed finite-valued state function independent of episode actions; preserving the mean does not assert variance reduction for every baseline.

Actor and critic updates both use pre-update parameters; terminal continuation is zero, I starts at one and is multiplied by γ, and admissibility requires domain preservation and almost-sure termination of the adaptive procedure.

load_bearing.statement: Each policy mass is totally differentiable on an open parameter domain; each state has a fixed nonempty support with positive masses throughout the domain, and the score on that support is ∇θ log πθ(a|s).

Under the stated finite-MDP, AC, fixed-support, neighborhood termination, dominated trajectory-differentiation and double-sum integrability hypotheses, J is totally differentiable at θ₀ and ∇J(θ₀) = Eθ₀[Σ_{t<T} γ^t G_t ∇θ log πθ₀(A_t|S_t)].
Under the stated AC, finite-model, fixed-support policy and terminating-episode hypotheses, Eθ[ψ_t|H_t] = 0 almost surely for every t ≥ 0, coordinate by coordinate, with ψ_t = 0 after termination.

Under the episodic policy-gradient theorem's hypotheses at θ₀, any fixed finite-valued state baseline chosen independently of episode actions satisfies Eθ₀[Σ_{t<T} γ^t(G_t-b(S_t))∇θ log πθ₀(A_t|S_t)] = ∇J(θ₀).

For the specified admissible adaptive episode, compute δ = R + γC − V̂_w(S), using zero terminal continuation, and update θ′ = θ + αIδ∇θ log πθ(A|S) and w′ = w + βδ∇w V̂_w(S) from the same pre-update parameters.
